{"command": "cat << 'EOF' > generate_3d_bar_plot.py
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import Axes3D

# Set random state for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

# Generate random data for y=k layers
num_bars = 30
colors = ['purple', 'orange', 'grey', 'pink']

# Create figure and 3D axis
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')

# Generate random data for each y=k layer
for i, color in enumerate(colors):
    y_layer = i  # y=k layer
    z_values = np.random.rand(num_bars)  # Random z values
    
    # Plot bars for this y=k layer
    for j in range(num_bars):
        # Use black for the last bar of each set
        bar_color = 'black' if j == num_bars - 1 else color
        ax.bar3d(
            j, y_layer, 0,  # x, y, z positions
            0.8, 0.8, z_values[j],  # dx, dy, dz dimensions
            color=bar_color,
            alpha=0.8,  # 80% opacity
            edgecolor='black'
        )

# Label axes
ax.set_xlabel('X Values (0-29)', labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Y Layers (Discrete)', labelpad=10)
ax.set_zlabel('Z Values (Random)', labelpad=10)

# Set y-axis ticks to only show discrete values where data is available
y_ticks = [0, 1, 2, 3]  # Corresponding to the colors
ax.set_yticks(y_ticks)
ax.set_yticklabels([f'y={k}' for k in y_ticks])

# Set x-axis limits and ticks
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, num_bars - 0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(num_bars))

# Set z-axis limits
max_z = np.max(np.random.rand(num_bars * 4))  # Approximate max z value
ax.set_zlim(0, max_z * 1.1)

# Add title
ax.set_title('3D Bar Plot with Y=k Layers', pad=20)

# Save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('figure.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
EOF"}

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import Axes3D

# Set random state for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

# Generate random data for y=k layers
num_bars = 30
colors = ['purple', 'orange', 'grey', 'pink']

# Create figure and 3D axis
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')

# Generate random data for each y=k layer
for i, color in enumerate(colors):
    y_layer = i  # y=k layer
    z_values = np.random.rand(num_bars)  # Random z values
    
    # Plot bars for this y=k layer
    for j in range(num_bars):
        # Use black for the last bar of each set
        bar_color = 'black' if j == num_bars - 1 else color
        ax.bar3d(
            j, y_layer, 0,  # x, y, z positions
            0.8, 0.8, z_values[j],  # dx, dy, dz dimensions
            color=bar_color,
            alpha=0.8,  # 80% opacity
            edgecolor='black'
        )

# Label axes
ax.set_xlabel('X Values (0-29)', labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Y Layers (Discrete)', labelpad=10)
ax.set_zlabel('Z Values (Random)', labelpad=10)

# Set y-axis ticks to only show discrete values where data is available
y_ticks = [0, 1, 2, 3]  # Corresponding to the colors
ax.set_yticks(y_ticks)
ax.set_yticklabels([f'y={k}' for k in y_ticks])

# Set x-axis limits and ticks
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, num_bars - 0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(num_bars))

# Set z-axis limits
max_z = np.max(np.random.rand(num_bars * 4))  # Approximate max z value
ax.set_zlim(0, max_z * 1.1)

# Add title
ax.set_title('3D Bar Plot with Y=k Layers', pad=20)

# Save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('figure.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
EOF
